newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma votes to condemn Russian government reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Duma votes to condemn Russian government reshuffle.

text.p: Russia's communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament on Wednesday condemned a government reshuffle ordered by President Boris Yeltsin to improve cabinet performance and force ahead economic reform.

The Duma voted by 230 to 122 in support of a non-binding resolution describing the reshuffle as a sign of the Kremlin's commitment to policies that would bring "national catastrophe". In the personnel changes, the cabinet is to be reinforced by reformist ministers.
Yeltsin blasted his government in his state of the nation address last week for failing to tackle a growing social and economic crisis.
But parliament was outraged by Yeltsin's decision to name his reformist chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, a hate-figure for communists, as first deputy prime minister.
The Duma was also angry that Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was given a free hand to shape the new government.
It demanded that Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin hold consultations with parliament on candidates for key cabinet posts. The resolution, however, is not binding on either the president or the government.
